card.name: Words leading into a result or reaction
card.fires_on: Marks a word just before a stated effect or outcome, such as the start of 'precipitate' after 'will' or 'may', or 'in' before 'particulate formation'. It also fires partway through some drug names.

modes.label: Start of 'precipitate'
modes.description: The first part of 'precipitate' after 'will' or 'may' in warnings about opioid antagonists causing withdrawal.
modes.example: administration of the recommended usual dosage of the antagonist will<< precip>>itate an acute withdrawal syndrome.

modes.label: Cause-to-effect links
modes.description: A small linking word or verb that leads into an outcome, such as 'result in' or 'without inducing'.
modes.example: Use of other diluents is not recommended because they may result<< in>> particulate formation.

modes.label: Inside drug names
modes.description: A middle piece of a long drug name.

card.plain: It fires on words that lead into an effect, mostly 'precipitate' in withdrawal warnings, and on some drug-name pieces.
